spec.description: Ecuador's hydrometeorological network read live: what the service says is transmitting, and what each station actually answers when asked.

options.content:
# Station network health — INAMHI

Ecuador's hydrometeorological network, read live from the API behind INAMHI's own
[Visor Hidrometeorológico](https://inamhi.gob.ec/info/). **1,894 stations** are on the books; the
service labels **224** of them as transmitting.

That label is what this dashboard is about. It is the network's own account of itself, and it is
not quite true: a station marked *TRANSMITIENDO* can be ten hours behind, some return no sensor
list at all, and eighteen of them are **manual** stations, which by definition cannot transmit.

This tab shows the label. **Reality check** stops trusting it and asks each hydrological station
directly. **Station** opens one box up, sensor by sensor. **Forecast** leaves the network aside and
shows what INAMHI tells the public.

The filters at the top cross all of it: status, province, owner, kind. Nothing here is stored or
pre-computed — every panel is a live call.

spec.title: The network on paper
spec.description: Straight from the inventory call, and cut by the filters above: what exists, and what the service says is alive.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
SELECT
  count(*)                                                             AS "Stations",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO') AS "Transmitting",
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO')
        / nullif(count(*), 0), 1)                                      AS "Share (%)",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
                     AND (e->>'categoria') LIKE '%HIDRO%')             AS "Hydrological"
FROM inv
  WHERE ($transmite = 'Todas' OR (e->>'estado_transmision') = $transmite)
    AND ((e->>'provincia')   IN (${provincia:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'propietario') IN (${propietario:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))

spec.title: The network as INAMHI labels it
spec.description: Every station the filters leave standing, coloured by the transmission status the service publishes. One request, up to 1,894 points. The layer list has two more readings of the same points: by kind, and by how they are read — which is where the eighteen manual 'transmitting' stations hide.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que

)
-- El mapa se sirve por DuckDB y no por Infinity justamente para que los filtros
-- de arriba lo recorten a él también: una URL fija no sabe filtrar, un WHERE sí.

       (e->>'longitud')::DOUBLE AS longitude,
       e->>'codigo'             AS code,

FROM inv
  WHERE ($transmite = 'Todas' OR (e->>'estado_transmision') = $transmite)
    AND ((e->>'provincia')   IN (${provincia:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'propietario') IN (${propietario:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))

spec.title: Stations by province
spec.description: Follows every filter above, the status one included: leave Status on All and this is the whole inventory; set it to Transmitting and it becomes the map of where the network is still alive — Pichincha alone holds almost a third of it.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
-- Obedece a TODOS los filtros, el de estado incluido. Antes forzaba
-- TRANSMITIENDO por dentro y el título mentía en cuanto alguien tocaba el
-- desplegable: contaba todas y seguía diciendo "las vivas".
SELECT e->>'provincia' AS key, count(*) AS n
FROM inv
  WHERE ($transmite = 'Todas' OR (e->>'estado_transmision') = $transmite)
    AND ((e->>'provincia')   IN (${provincia:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'propietario') IN (${propietario:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 12

spec.title: Who keeps them running
spec.description: Stations by owner, split into what still transmits and what does not. INAMHI is not the only keeper: CELEC, EPMAPS and the old EX-INERHI hold a large share of the books.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
-- Apilado a propósito: la barra entera es el total de ese dueño y el tramo verde
-- lo que sigue vivo. Con dos series sueltas, 224 al lado de 1.500 era una raya.
SELECT e->>'propietario' AS key,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO')  AS "Transmitting",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') <> 'TRANSMITIENDO') AS "Silent"
FROM inv
  WHERE ($transmite = 'Todas' OR (e->>'estado_transmision') = $transmite)
    AND ((e->>'provincia')   IN (${provincia:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'propietario') IN (${propietario:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY "Transmitting" + "Silent" DESC
LIMIT 10

spec.title: The eighteen impossible ones
spec.description: Stations whose sensing is MANUAL — someone walks up and reads the instrument — and which the same row marks as transmitting. Both fields come from the inventory as they are. They are left out of the freshness tab on purpose: for a manual station `fecha_ultimo_dato` is not the age of the data (M1208 said the 17th at 18:02 while its newest reading was from the 15th at 12:05).

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
-- Una contradicción que el propio inventario publica: estaciones cuyo captor es
-- MANUAL —alguien va, lee el instrumento y lo anota— marcadas como que
-- TRANSMITEN. Son 18 de las 224. No es un error de lectura nuestro: los dos
-- campos vienen así en la misma fila.
--
-- Y sí responden a `parametros/`, pero con otra trampa encima: ahí
-- `fecha_ultimo_dato` NO es la edad del dato. Medido el 2026-09-17 en M1208,
-- decía «17 a las 18:02» mientras su último dato real era del «15 a las 12:05».
-- Por eso estas estaciones se quedan fuera de la pestaña que mide frescura.
SELECT e->>'codigo'      AS "Code",
       e->>'punto_obs'   AS "Station",
       e->>'categoria'   AS "Kind",
       e->>'provincia'   AS "Province",
       e->>'propietario' AS "Owner"
FROM inv
WHERE (e->>'captor') = 'MANUAL'
  AND (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
ORDER BY "Province", "Code"

options.content:
**Source** — INAMHI, *Visor Hidrometeorológico* (`inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor`), read live.
Forecast discharge from **GEOGLOWS** and the daily outlook from `api_pronos`, both served by INAMHI.
Live rainfall from **GEOGLOWS**' PERSIANN, over WMS.

**What the numbers do not say.** *Transmitting* is the organisation's own label and is not a
measurement: the *Reality check* tab is. Public history is capped at **ten days** — a longer range
returns 401, not an error a panel can explain. Timestamps in the sensor listing arrive tagged
`-05:00` on a clock that is really UTC, so every panel corrects it rather than repeating it. And a
handful of stations report impossible rainfall — a sensor fault the service passes through
unfiltered — so a single station's spike is not evidence of weather.

### Measured, not labelled

Everything on this tab asks the stations themselves. For each hydrological station that claims to
be transmitting, one call fetches its sensor list and the newest timestamp in it; the age is
computed against UTC. **It takes 8 to 11 seconds** — 43 calls, one per station, because the API has
no bulk endpoint for freshness and `parametros/` without a station answers 400. The tab only pays
that when you open it.

Green is under three hours, which is as fresh as an hourly network gets. Red is over six: a station
that says it is alive and is not keeping up. A station with **no sensors at all** keeps its row,
with an empty age — losing those would hide exactly what this tab is for.

spec.title: Measured, not labelled — the hydrological stations
spec.description: The hydrological stations that claim to be transmitting, each asked directly how old its newest reading is. Anything red says it is alive and is not keeping up.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
),
-- Las hidrológicas que DICEN transmitir, ya recortadas por los filtros de arriba.
-- Cada una se pregunta por separado: no existe endpoint que dé la frescura de
-- toda la red de golpe (`parametros/` sin `id_estacion` responde 400).
hidro AS (
  SELECT (e->>'id_estacion')::BIGINT AS id_estacion,
         e->>'codigo'    AS codigo,
         e->>'punto_obs' AS nombre,
         e->>'provincia' AS provincia,
         (e->>'latitud')::DOUBLE  AS latitude,
         (e->>'longitud')::DOUBLE AS longitude
  FROM inv
  WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
    AND (e->>'categoria') LIKE '%HIDRO%'
    AND ((e->>'provincia')   IN (${provincia:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'propietario') IN (${propietario:singlequote}))
    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))
),
probed AS (
  SELECT h.*,
         http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || h.id_estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS r
  FROM hidro h
),
-- El `coalesce` de dos pisos es el que salva a los muertos: una estación que
-- devuelve cuerpo vacío se queda con lista vacía en vez de desaparecer. Con un
-- LATERAL/unnest en su lugar, esas filas se esfuman sin avisar — justo las que
-- esta pestaña existe para enseñar.
medido AS (
  SELECT codigo, nombre, provincia, latitude, longitude, (r->>'status') AS status,
         coalesce(
           json_extract_string(coalesce(nullif(r->>'body', ''), '[]'),
                               '$[*].params[*].fecha_ultimo_dato'),
           []::VARCHAR[]) AS sellos
  FROM probed
),
-- `fecha_ultimo_dato` llega etiquetada `-05:00`, pero ese reloj ES UTC: si se
-- creyera el sufijo, el último dato caería cinco horas en el futuro. Se corta a
-- 19 caracteres y se compara contra UTC.
fechas AS (
  SELECT *, list_max(list_transform(sellos,
             s -> strptime(s[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'))) AS ultimo
  FROM medido
)
SELECT codigo      AS "Code",
       nombre      AS "Station",
       provincia   AS "Province",
       len(sellos) AS "Sensors",
       ultimo      AS "Last datum (UTC)",
       round(date_diff('minute', ultimo, timezone('UTC', now())) / 60.0, 1) AS "Hours behind"
FROM fechas
ORDER BY "Hours behind" DESC NULLS FIRST

spec.description: The only layer on this dashboard that draws what was checked rather than what was declared. Grey is a station that answered nothing at all.

    AND ((e->>'categoria')   IN (${categoria:singlequote}))

                  || h.id_estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS r
  FROM hidro h

-- devuelve cuerpo vacío se queda con lista vacía en vez de desaparecer. Con un
-- LATERAL/unnest en su lugar, esas filas se esfuman sin avisar — justo las que
-- esta pestaña existe para enseñar.
medido AS (
  SELECT codigo, nombre, provincia, latitude, longitude, (r->>'status') AS status,
         coalesce(
           json_extract_string(coalesce(nullif(r->>'body', ''), '[]'),
                               '$[*].params[*].fecha_ultimo_dato'),
           []::VARCHAR[]) AS sellos
  FROM probed
),
-- `fecha_ultimo_dato` llega etiquetada `-05:00`, pero ese reloj ES UTC: si se
-- creyera el sufijo, el último dato caería cinco horas en el futuro. Se corta a
-- 19 caracteres y se compara contra UTC.

             s -> strptime(s[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'))) AS ultimo

            WHEN horas < 6     THEN 'lagging'

FROM (
  SELECT latitude, longitude, codigo AS codage, nombre, provincia,
         round(date_diff('minute', ultimo, timezone('UTC', now())) / 60.0, 1) AS horas
  FROM fechas
)

options.content:
### One station, opened up

The charts below are **one per magnitude**, not one per sensor — the service publishes most
readings three times over (maximum, mean and minimum), so a panel per entry would be thirty-three
lines of nothing. Each chart carries its magnitude's three statistics together.

*Transmitting* is a property of the box, not of its sensors: the table shows stations an hour fresh
on rainfall and years stale on soil temperature, in the same cabinet. **Battery** is the one reading
that is about the station rather than the weather — about two in five report it, and a sagging
charge is what precedes a station going quiet.

spec.title: Sensor by sensor
spec.description: Every sensor in the chosen station and how far behind each one is.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- Los sensores de la estación elegida, con lo viejo que es el dato de cada uno.
-- Aquí se ve que "transmitiendo" es una propiedad de la ESTACIÓN y no de sus
-- sensores: en una misma caja conviven el pluviómetro de hace una hora y la
-- sonda de suelo parada desde 2016.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || $estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS resp
), s AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    coalesce(nullif(resp->>'body', ''), '[]'), '$[*].params[*]')) AS p
  FROM r
)
SELECT p->>'descripcion_parametro' AS "Sensor",
       p->>'simbolo_unidad'        AS "Unit",
       strptime((p->>'fecha_ultimo_dato')[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S') AS "Last datum (UTC)",
       round(date_diff('minute',
             strptime((p->>'fecha_ultimo_dato')[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'),
             timezone('UTC', now())) / 60.0, 1) AS "Hours behind"
FROM s
ORDER BY "Hours behind"

spec.title: Battery
spec.description: Supply voltage, where the station reports it — about two in five do. The daily sawtooth is a solar panel charging; a falling floor night after night is a station about to go quiet.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- Un panel por MAGNITUD, no por sensor. La diferencia importa: Gualaceo no tiene
-- doce sensores sino treinta y tres entradas, porque cada magnitud aparece por
-- triplicado (MAX, PROM, MIN). Repetir por entrada daría treinta y tres paneles
-- de una línea; repetir por magnitud da doce con su banda máximo-mínimo y la
-- media dentro, que es como se lee una variable meteorológica.
--
-- Por eso la consulta pide primero los códigos de ESTA magnitud y luego los pide
-- todos juntos en un solo POST.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || $estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS resp
), grupos AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    coalesce(nullif(resp->>'body', ''), '[]'), '$[*]')) AS g
  FROM r
), mio AS (
  SELECT g FROM grupos WHERE (g->>'id_param') = '39'
), pedido AS (
  -- El mapa de cabeceras va VACÍO a propósito: `http_post` ya pone el suyo
  -- `application/json`, y añadirlo otra vez manda «application/json,
  -- application/json» y el servicio contesta 415 Unsupported Media Type.
  --
  -- Y las fechas van con BARRAS: con guiones, 500 y página de Django.
  SELECT http_post(
    'https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_data_automaticas/get_data_hour/',
    MAP {},
    json_object(
      'id_estacion',  CAST($estacion AS BIGINT),
      -- Solo los códigos HORARIOS. El grupo de precipitación trae también el
      -- acumulado diario (`017140801d`), y pedir un diario y un horario juntos a
      -- `get_data_hour` devuelve 500: el panel entero se quedaba en "No data".
      'table_names',  list_filter(json_extract_string(g, '$.params[*].nemonico'),
                                  n -> n LIKE '%h'),
      'fecha_desde',  strftime($__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ, '%Y/%m/%d'),
      'fecha_hasta',  strftime($__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ,   '%Y/%m/%d'))
  ) AS resp
  FROM mio
), ok AS (
  SELECT resp->>'body' AS body FROM pedido WHERE (resp->>'status') = '200'
), ser AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(body, '$.series[*]')) AS s FROM ok
)
SELECT (d->>'date')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
       (d->>'value')::DOUBLE     AS value,
       CASE s->>'measure_type' WHEN 'PROM' THEN 'mean'  WHEN 'MAX'  THEN 'max'
                               WHEN 'MIN'  THEN 'min'   WHEN 'SUM'  THEN 'sum'
                               WHEN 'INST' THEN 'value' ELSE lower(s->>'measure_type') END AS metric
FROM ser, LATERAL (SELECT unnest(json_extract(s, '$.data[*]')) AS d) t
ORDER BY time

spec.title: ${magnitud}
spec.description: One chart per magnitude, with its statistics together: the band is maximum to minimum and the line through it the mean. Repeated over every magnitude the chosen station still reports.

      'table_names',  list_filter(json_extract_string(g, '$.params[*].nemonico'),
                                  n -> n LIKE '%h'),
      'fecha_desde',  strftime($__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ, '%Y/%m/%d'),
      'fecha_hasta',  strftime($__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ,   '%Y/%m/%d'))
  ) AS resp
  FROM mio
), ok AS (
  SELECT resp->>'body' AS body FROM pedido WHERE (resp->>'status') = '200'
), ser AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(body, '$.series[*]')) AS s FROM ok
)
SELECT (d->>'date')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
       (d->>'value')::DOUBLE     AS value,
       CASE s->>'measure_type' WHEN 'PROM' THEN 'mean'  WHEN 'MAX'  THEN 'max'
                               WHEN 'MIN'  THEN 'min'   WHEN 'SUM'  THEN 'sum'
                               WHEN 'INST' THEN 'value' ELSE lower(s->>'measure_type') END AS metric
FROM ser, LATERAL (SELECT unnest(json_extract(s, '$.data[*]')) AS d) t
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Forecast discharge — GEOGLOWS
spec.description: Fifteen days of modelled discharge for the river reach attached to this station, three-hourly, with its uncertainty band. The dashboard window reaches into the future so this has somewhere to be drawn: measurement stops at now, the forecast carries on. Only hydrological stations with a reach return anything; for the rest this panel is empty, which is the service's own answer and not a failure.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- GEOGLOWS solo contesta por las estaciones que tienen un tramo de río asociado
-- —27 de las 651 hidrológicas—; al resto les responde 404 con su motivo:
-- "La estación no tiene un river_id asociado". Ese 404 es la respuesta CORRECTA,
-- no una avería, así que el guardián de estado lo convierte en cero filas en vez
-- de en un aspa roja que contradiría la descripción del panel.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/geoglows/forecast/station/' || $estacion || '/') AS resp
), ok AS (
  SELECT resp->>'body' AS body FROM r WHERE (resp->>'status') = '200'
), pts AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(body, '$.data[*]')) AS d FROM ok
)
SELECT (d->>'date')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
       (d->>'median')::DOUBLE    AS median,
       (d->>'lower')::DOUBLE     AS lower,
       (d->>'upper')::DOUBLE     AS upper
FROM pts
ORDER BY time

options.content:
### What the public is told

INAMHI's daily outlook for the 26 provincial capitals, from a different API to everything else on
this dashboard. Underneath it, the rain a satellite actually saw: **PERSIANN**, served by GEOGLOWS
over WMS and driven by the map's own clock.

Put together they answer a question the station map cannot: the forecast says one thing, the
satellite saw another, and the gauges on the other tabs are what would settle it — if enough of
them were still reporting.

spec.title: Tomorrow, as announced — and the rain already falling
spec.description: The 26 provincial capitals with their outlook, over PERSIANN's live rainfall. The map builds the rainfall layer by itself as soon as it recognises a `wms_url` column, and its clock chooses which pass to draw.

spec.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- Otra API distinta —`api_pronos`, no `api_visor`— y la única del tablero que no
-- habla de estaciones sino de ciudades: las 26 capitales, con coordenada. Es lo
-- que ve el público cuando mira el tiempo.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_pronos/forecast/daily_forecast/list_by_date_now/') AS resp
), loc AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(resp->>'body', '$[*]')) AS l
  FROM r WHERE (resp->>'status') = '200'
), periodos AS (
  -- Las cuatro franjas se giran a columnas por NOMBRE y no por posición: que el
  -- array venga siempre en el mismo orden no lo garantiza nadie.
  SELECT l,
         max(CASE WHEN p->>'period_name' = 'Madrugada' THEN p->>'condition_name' END) AS madrugada,
         max(CASE WHEN p->>'period_name' = 'Mañana'    THEN p->>'condition_name' END) AS manana,
         max(CASE WHEN p->>'period_name' = 'Tarde'     THEN p->>'condition_name' END) AS tarde,
         max(CASE WHEN p->>'period_name' = 'Noche'     THEN p->>'condition_name' END) AS noche
  FROM loc, LATERAL (SELECT unnest(json_extract(l, '$.forecast[*]')) AS p) t
  GROUP BY l
)
SELECT l->>'locality_name'    AS locality,
       l->>'fk_province_name' AS province,
       (l->>'latitude')::DOUBLE        AS latitude,
       (l->>'longitude')::DOUBLE       AS longitude,
       (l->>'min_temperature')::DOUBLE AS min_c,
       (l->>'max_temperature')::DOUBLE AS max_c,
       (l->>'uv_radiation')::INTEGER   AS uv,
       CASE WHEN (l->>'rain')::BOOLEAN THEN 'rain' ELSE 'dry' END AS rain,
       madrugada AS small_hours, manana AS morning,
       tarde     AS afternoon,   noche  AS night
FROM periodos
ORDER BY province

LOAD http_client;
-- La lluvia que el satélite ve AHORA, debajo del pronóstico. Las fechas las
-- publica el propio servicio en su GetCapabilities: la consulta no inventa un
-- calendario, lo lee. El panel monta la capa él solo en cuanto reconoce una
-- columna `wms_url`.
WITH caps AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://services.geoglows.org/geoserver/satellite_based_precipitation/wms'
                  || '?service=WMS&request=GetCapabilities')->>'body' AS xml
), extent AS (
  SELECT regexp_extract(
    xml,
    '(?s)<Name>persiann_pdir_24h</Name>.*?<Dimension name="time"[^>]*>([^<]*)</Dimension>',
    1) AS times
  FROM caps
), fechas AS (
  -- En su propia etapa: DuckDB no admite UNNEST en un SELECT que además filtra.
  SELECT unnest(str_split(times, ','))::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time FROM extent
)
SELECT time,
       'https://services.geoglows.org/geoserver/satellite_based_precipitation/wms' AS wms_url,
       'persiann_pdir_24h' AS wms_layer
FROM fechas
WHERE time BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ AND $__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ
ORDER BY time

spec.name: provincia
spec.label: Province
spec.description: Crosses every panel. The station picker on the third tab obeys it too, so choosing a province narrows what you can drill into.
spec.definition:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
SELECT DISTINCT (e->>'provincia') AS __text, (e->>'provincia') AS __value
FROM inv WHERE (e->>'provincia') IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

spec.name: magnitud
spec.label: Magnitudes
spec.description: What the station still measures, and what the charts on its tab repeat over. Sensors with nothing newer than thirty days are left out.
spec.definition:
LOAD http_client;
-- El filtro de treinta días no es cosmético: hay cajas que siguen publicando
-- sondas de suelo paradas en 2016, y sin él encabezan la lista de paneles.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || '${estacion}' || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS resp
), g AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    coalesce(nullif(resp->>'body', ''), '[]'), '$[*]')) AS grp
  FROM r
), vivas AS (
  SELECT grp,
         list_max(list_transform(
           coalesce(json_extract_string(grp, '$.params[*].fecha_ultimo_dato'), []::VARCHAR[]),
           s -> strptime(s[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'))) AS ultimo
  FROM g
)
SELECT (grp->>'name_param') || ' (' || (grp->>'simbolo_unidad') || ')' AS __text,
       (grp->>'id_param')                                              AS __value
FROM vivas
WHERE ultimo > timezone('UTC', now()) - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  -- El voltaje de la batería queda fuera: tiene panel propio arriba y repetirlo
  -- aquí lo dibujaba dos veces en la misma pestaña.
  AND (grp->>'id_param') <> '39'
ORDER BY __text
